 JMU football (7-2, 5-2 Sun Belt) fell short to Troy (4-4, 2-2) 24-21 at Bridgeforth Stadium Thursday night. The Dukes haven’t dropped two back-to-back games since November 2024.
 Here’s what you need to know:
 JMU capitalized on its first drive of the game. After key plays from fifth-year running back Seth Cromwell and fourth-year wide receiver Braeden Wisloski gained yards for the Dukes, fourth-year wide receiver Corey Scott scored a 2-yard touchdown at 8:57. 
 The Dukes kept momentum up, finding the end zone just over four minutes later. A 33-yard pass from fourth-year quarterback Camden Coleman found Wisloski to put JMU up 14. 
 Troy opened up the second quarter in the end zone on a 1-yard rush from third-year running back Gavin Griffin to get it on the board. 
 Cromwell recorded his third touchdown of the season on a 14-yard rush at 8:41 in the second. 
 Opening up the second half, a pass from third-year quarterback JC Evans at 14:26 during the third was intercepted and returned for a touchdown by fifth-year safety Justin Powe at 14:26.
 After a fumble from second-year wide receiver Jeremiah Harrison was fumbled and recovered by Troy, third-year running back Jaheim Merriweather notched a 28-yard touchdown to even the score at 21 at 6:25 during the third.
 Troy’s attempt to push ahead on a 49-yard field goal fell short. 
 After an unsuccessful overtime drive, Troy came back and knocked in a 27-yard field goal to secure the win. 
 JMU hits the road to face Southern Miss at 8 p.m. EST on Thursday, Nov. 5.
